title: Testing and Code Quality
description: Choose test strategies and improve reliability through feedback.

questions.prompt: What is a unit test intended to verify?
options: A small component in isolation or with controlled collaborators
questions.explanation: Unit tests focus on small units with dependencies controlled to provide fast, localized feedback.

questions.prompt: What does an integration test primarily check?
options: A single function with all dependencies mocked
questions.explanation: Integration tests exercise boundaries where components work together, such as a service and database.

questions.prompt: End-to-end tests typically exercise a user-visible flow across multiple system layers.
questions.explanation: They validate integrated behavior but are often slower and more environment-sensitive than unit tests.

questions.prompt: Why favor many fast tests and fewer broad end-to-end tests?
options: Fast focused tests provide quicker, more localized feedback
Unit tests prove the entire system correct
The pyramid is a required file structure
questions.explanation: A balanced suite uses inexpensive tests broadly and reserves slower integrated tests for critical flows.

questions.prompt: Which are common test doubles?
questions.explanation: Stubs, mocks, and fakes replace collaborators in tests; backups are data artifacts, not test-double types.

questions.prompt: What is a risk of overusing mocks?
options: Tests can become coupled to implementation details
Tests become impossible to run locally
questions.explanation: Brittle interaction-heavy tests may fail after harmless refactoring without validating user-visible behavior.

questions.prompt: Why test boundary values?
options: Defects often occur at limits and transitions between cases
Boundaries are always the most common inputs
It removes the need to test typical cases
questions.explanation: Off-by-one and range errors often occur at boundaries such as zero, maximum, or empty input.

questions.prompt: What is characteristic of property-based testing?
options: Generate many inputs from a defined space
Shrink failing cases in some frameworks
Require a handwritten expected output for every generated case
questions.explanation: Property-based tools generate cases, check invariants, and can minimize failures to simpler examples.

questions.prompt: What is a regression test?
options: A test that checks previously working behavior remains correct after changes
A test run only before the first release
questions.explanation: Regression tests guard against reintroducing defects or breaking established behavior.

questions.prompt: 100% line coverage proves that a program is free of defects.
questions.explanation: Coverage shows executed code, not whether assertions are adequate or all relevant behavior is correct.

questions.prompt: What does mutation testing assess?
options: Whether tests detect small intentional changes to the code
questions.explanation: Mutation testing introduces small code changes and checks whether tests fail, probing assertion effectiveness.

questions.prompt: What does static analysis examine?
options: Source code without executing the program
A binary after every possible input
questions.explanation: Static analyzers inspect code for patterns, defects, or policy violations without running it.

questions.prompt: Which practices improve code review effectiveness?
options: Explain the intent and relevant context
Require reviewers to approve without reading
questions.explanation: Focused changes and clear context enable meaningful review of behavior and maintainability.

questions.prompt: What is the primary purpose of continuous integration?
options: Frequently integrate changes and run automated checks
Deploy every commit to production without controls
Avoid testing locally or in CI
questions.explanation: CI provides rapid feedback by building and testing integrated changes regularly.

questions.prompt: A flaky test has inconsistent results under apparently equivalent conditions.
questions.explanation: Flakiness undermines trust in test signals and should be investigated rather than ignored.

questions.prompt: Why isolate tests from shared mutable state?
options: Increase the number of source files
questions.explanation: Isolation makes outcomes more deterministic and prevents one test from affecting another.

questions.prompt: What does a contract test verify?
options: An agreed interaction between a provider and consumer
questions.explanation: Contract tests check that a service provider and its consumers agree on interface expectations.

questions.prompt: Which information helps triage a reported defect?
options: A guess presented as verified root cause
questions.explanation: Reproduction, observed behavior, and environment provide actionable evidence; hypotheses should be labeled as such.

questions.prompt: What is a code smell?
options: A sign that design may benefit from review or refactoring
questions.explanation: Smells suggest possible maintainability problems but do not by themselves prove incorrect behavior.

questions.prompt: What is refactoring?
options: Restructure code without changing its externally observable behavior
Add a new feature with no tests
Rewrite all source in another language
questions.explanation: Refactoring improves internal structure while preserving behavior, ideally protected by tests.
